title: Tensor, Hom and projection normalization for a cohomological comparison
statement:
Fix two correspondences $c,\bar c$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, and a compactifiable cohomological pre-comparison $(f_Z,t_Z,\alpha_g,\beta_g,\iota)$ of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. Use its $j_Z,r_Z,d_Z,\delta_Z,\Pi$ and ordinary and exceptional mates, and the dualizing complexes of [def-trf-dualizing-complex]. All tensor products, pullbacks and internal Homs are derived. For each diagram arrow $g:U\to V$, write $T_g:g^!M\otimes g^*N\to g^!(M\otimes N)$ for the exceptional tensor map: its $Rg_!\dashv g^!$ adjunct is $Rg_!(g^!M\otimes g^*N)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_g^{-1}}Rg_!g^!M\otimes N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_g^!\otimes1}M\otimes N$, using [def-exchange-projection, prop-functor-package, def-trf-admissibility]. Write $H_g:g^!R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\to R\mathcal Hom(g^*M,g^!N)$ for its tensor--Hom transpose followed by evaluation. Barred versions use $\bar g$. For every pair of objects in the indicated finite-Tor constructible domains the following identities hold.

(a) Exceptional tensor compatibility:
$$\beta_g(M\otimes N)\circ f_U(T_g)\circ t_U\circ(1\otimes\alpha_g)=\bar g^!(t_V)\circ T_{\bar g}\circ(\beta_g\otimes1)$$
as maps $f_Ug^!M\otimes\bar g^*f_VN\to\bar g^!f_V(M\otimes N)$.

(b) Exceptional internal-Hom compatibility:
$$R\mathcal Hom(\alpha_g,\beta_g)\circ r_U\circ f_U(H_g)=H_{\bar g}\circ\bar g^!(r_V)\circ\beta_g$$
as maps $f_Ug^!R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\to R\mathcal Hom(\bar g^*f_VM,\bar g^!f_VN)$.

(c) Tensor unit and diagonal normalization:
$$t_Z\circ(1\otimes j_Z)=1_{f_ZM},\qquad\alpha_\Delta\circ\bar\Delta^*\Pi_{M,N}=t_X,$$
with $f_ZM\otimes A_{\bar Z}=f_ZM$ and $\Delta^*(M\boxtimes N)=M\otimes N$ [def-trf-external-product].

(d) Put $\chi:p_2^*\omega_X\to p_1^!A_X$ for the canonical exchange in the Cartesian square $X\times_kX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ over $s$ (the leg order is the project's order). More explicitly, put $B_M=(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,a,a}(M))^{-1}:Rp_{1!}p_2^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a_X^*Ra_{X!}M$, where the compact-support exchange is normalized as in [def-exchange-projection] and is invertible by [prop-functor-package](4). Define $\chi$ to be the $Rp_{1!}\dashv p_1^!$ transpose of $a_X^*(\varepsilon_{a_X,A_s}^!)\circ B_{\omega_X}$. Its barred counterpart is defined by the identical formula for the barred operations. Then
$$\beta_{p_1}(A_X)\circ f_{X\times X}(\chi)\circ\alpha_{p_2}(\omega_X)=p_{1,\bar X}^!(j_X)\circ\bar\chi\circ p_{2,\bar X}^*(\delta_X)$$
as maps $p_{2,\bar X}^*f_X\omega_X\to p_{1,\bar X}^!f_XA_X$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2(a),(b) and Lemma 4.2.4(b),(e),(f), with the two projection indices interchanged

proof.text: We prove (a) first. Use requirement (VII) of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] to extend the diagrams and comparison maps to the proper compactifications. The compactified product $X^*\times_sX^*$ is proper over $s$: its projection is the base change of $a_{X^*}$, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and its structure map is a proper composite by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Also $F^*=\operatorname{Fix}(c^*)$ is proper: it is the inverse image of $\Delta_{X^*}$ by [def-trf-fixed-scheme]; that diagonal is closed because $X^*$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; its base change is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; and a closed subscheme of proper $C^*$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c). The barred argument applies those same four statements to $\bar X^*,\bar C^*$. Thus every compactified object is proper over $s$ and separated, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes every diagram arrow proper. This reduction applies to arbitrary input complexes, not only to ones initially specified on the compactifications: for an open $j:V\hookrightarrow V^*$ extend each input $M,N$ by $j_!$, which stays in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [lem-trf-open-ctf], and whose restriction is the input by the open-unit isomorphism of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Ordinary pullback and tensor restrict by their composition comparisons; exceptional pullback restricts by the canonical identification $j^!=j^*$: [prop-exc-open-adjoint] gives $j_!\dashv j^*$, while [def-trf-admissibility] gives $j_!\dashv j^!$, so uniqueness of right adjoints identifies them; exceptional composition is then [def-trf-admissibility]. Internal Hom restricts by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. The identity/composition/exchange/projection coherence of [fix-prop-coherence] identifies the restrictions of the counit-defined tensor and product-square exchange maps with the original maps. Requirement (VII) identifies the restricted comparison data. Therefore equality on the extended inputs restricts to the asserted equality on the given inputs. On these proper diagrams put $a_g=\alpha_{g,*}$ and $b_g=\beta_{g,!}=a_g^{-1}$ by (VI). Write $\pi_g: Rg_*P\otimes N\to Rg_*(P\otimes g^*N)$ for the counit-defined projection map of [def-exchange-projection]. It is invertible on these finite-Tor domains by [prop-functor-package](5); its inverse will be denoted $Q_g$. The proper identifications in (3) identify these maps with the compact-support projection maps. The same notation with bars is used for the barred operations. All finite-stage complexes used here are bounded constructible and hence have etale-origin representatives by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii); this verifies the finite pro-etale domain required by clause (4) when it is used in Step 8.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2(a), initial compactification reduction and diagram (4.2)

proof.text:
The ordinary projection square needed for (a) is
$$R\bar g_*\bigl(t_U(1\otimes\alpha_g)\bigr)\,\bar\pi_g(a_g(P)\otimes1)
=a_g(P\otimes g^*N)\,f_V(\pi_g)\,t_V.$$
Both sides go from $f_VRg_*P\otimes f_VN$ to $R\bar g_*f_U(P\otimes g^*N)$. Take $\bar g^*\dashv R\bar g_*$ transposes. Using the defining transpose of $a_g$ and that of $\pi_g$ in [def-exchange-projection], the left transpose is
$$t_U\bigl((f_U\varepsilon_{g,P}\circ\alpha_g(Rg_*P))\otimes\alpha_g(N)\bigr).$$
For the right transpose, naturality of $\alpha_g$ moves $f_V\pi_g$ past $\alpha_g$, and (IV) replaces $\alpha_g\bar g^*t_V$ by $t_U(\alpha_g\otimes\alpha_g)$. The remaining counit composed with $g^*\pi_g$ is $\varepsilon_{g,P}\otimes1$, by the defining transpose of $\pi_g$ and the triangle identity. Naturality of $t_U$ then gives exactly the same displayed transpose. Bijectivity of adjunction proves the square. This is the expanded calculation behind diagram (4.3).

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2(a), left square of (4.2) and ordinary-adjoint diagram (4.3)

proof.text:
Invert the proper mates and projection maps in Step 2, obtaining
$$f_V(Q_g)\,b_g(P\otimes g^*N)\,R\bar g_!\bigl(t_U(1\otimes\alpha_g)\bigr)
=t_V(b_g(P)\otimes1)\,\bar Q_g.$$
Set $P=g^!M$ and let $\varepsilon_g^!$ denote the exceptional counit. The definition of $T_g$ says $\varepsilon_g^!\circ Rg_!T_g=(\varepsilon_g^!\otimes1)Q_g$. The mate definition of $b_g$ similarly gives
$$\varepsilon_{\bar g}^!\circ R\bar g_!\beta_g=f_V(\varepsilon_g^!)\circ b_g(g^!(-)).$$
Take exceptional adjoints of the two sides of (a) and substitute these formulas. Naturality of $b_g$ moves $R\bar g_!f_UT_g$ through $b_g$; the first adjunct becomes
$$f_V(\varepsilon_g^!\otimes1)\,f_V(Q_g)\,b_g(P\otimes g^*N)\,R\bar g_!\bigl(t_U(1\otimes\alpha_g)\bigr).$$
Step 2's inverted identity and naturality of $t_V$ turn this into
$$t_V\bigl((f_V\varepsilon_g^!)b_g(P)\otimes1\bigr)\bar Q_g,$$
which is the other adjunct by the barred definitions. Exceptional adjunction proves (a), and Step 1 restricts it back to the original diagrams.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2(a), right squares of (4.2) and conclusion

proof.text:
For (b), put $L=R\mathcal Hom(M,N)$ and $e:L\otimes M\to N$ for evaluation. Apply (a) to $(L,M)$, and then postcompose by $\bar g^!f_V(e)$. Naturality of $\beta_g$ yields the common map
$$\beta_g(N)\,f_U\bigl(g^!e\circ T_g(L,M)\bigr)\,t_U(1\otimes\alpha_g(M))$$
from $f_Ug^!L\otimes\bar g^*f_VM$ to $\bar g^!f_VN$. The defining uncurrying of $H_g$ is $g^!e\circ T_g(L,M)$, and the defining uncurrying of $r_U$ is $f_U\operatorname{ev}\circ t_U$. Thus the displayed map is the uncurrying of the left side of (b). On the other route of (a), naturality of $T_{\bar g}$ moves $\bar g^!r_V$ through the first tensor factor, and $\operatorname{ev}\circ(r_V\otimes1)=f_Ve\circ t_V$ identifies it with the uncurrying of the right side. The tensor–Hom bijection follows by combining the currying isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] with [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]. Its injectivity proves (b). All inputs are in the stated finite-Tor constructible domains.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2(b), diagram (4.4) and its tensor–Hom transposes

proof.text: For the unit part of (c), first write $\rho_L=t_Z(L,A_Z)(1\otimes j_Z)$ and prove $\delta_Z\rho_{\omega_Z}=\delta_Z$. By the compactification reduction of Step 1 it suffices to prove this on the compactified diagrams: by (VII) the restriction to $\bar Z$ of $t_{Z^*}$, $j_{Z^*}$ and $\delta_{Z^*}$ is $t_Z$, $j_Z$ and $\delta_Z$, and $u_Z^*\omega_{Z^*}=\omega_Z$ by exceptional composition and $u^!=u^*$. There $a_Z$ and $a_{\bar Z}$ are proper, so by [prop-functor-package](3) the compact-support projection map $\operatorname{PF}$ defining $T$ is the counit-defined projection map $\pi$ of [def-exchange-projection], as recorded in Step 1. Apply (a) with $g=a_Z$ and $M=N=A_s$. The maps $T_{a_Z}(A_s,A_s)$ and its barred counterpart become the identity under the tensor-unit identifications: the counit-defined projection map at the tensor unit is the unitor, since its ordinary adjunct is the counit; consequently the exceptional adjunct defining $T$ is $\varepsilon_{a_Z}^!$, whose transpose is the identity by the exceptional triangle identity. Precompose with $1\otimes a_{\bar Z}^*(\iota^{-1})$ and postcompose with $a_{\bar Z}^!\iota$. The left side becomes $\delta_Z\rho_{\omega_Z}$, because $j_Z=\alpha_{a_Z}(A_s)a_{\bar Z}^*(\iota^{-1})$. On the right, naturality of $T_{a_{\bar Z}}$ and (II), $\iota t_s=\iota\otimes\iota$, replace the coefficient factor by its unit identification and leave $a_{\bar Z}^!\iota\circ\beta_{a_Z}=\delta_Z$. This is the required dualizing-unit equation; scalar normalization alone would not prove the unit equation on arbitrary $f_ZL$.

Put $F=f_ZM$, $B=f_ZD_ZM$, and
$$E_M=\delta_Z\,f_Z(\operatorname{ev}_M)\,t_Z:B\otimes F\to\omega_{\bar Z}.$$
Associativity (I) first combines $t_Z(B,F)$ with $t_Z(F,A_Z)$; naturality at $\operatorname{ev}_M$ then gives
$$E_M(1\otimes\rho_M)=\delta_Z\rho_{\omega_Z}\,f_Z(\operatorname{ev}_M)t_Z=E_M$$
by Step 5. By the definition in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison], currying $E_M$ in the $B$ variable gives the isomorphism $d_Z(M):B\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\bar Z}F$ of (V). Currying in the other variable gives $F\to D_{\bar Z}B$, namely $D_{\bar Z}(d_Z(M))\circ\mathrm{bid}_F$, with signed symmetry inserted. Here $\mathrm{bid}_F$ is specifically the natural double-dual map obtained by transposing $\operatorname{ev}_F$; naturality of tensor--Hom transposition gives the displayed formula for the other transpose of $E_M$. It is an isomorphism by [thm-fix-general-biduality], which applies to $F\in D^b_{ctf}(\bar Z,A)$. Therefore the equality of evaluations says $\gamma\rho_M=\gamma$ for this isomorphism $\gamma:F\to D_{\bar Z}B$. Cancel $\gamma$ to obtain $\rho_M=1_F$, as required. No rigidity or site-perfect hypothesis on $M$ is used.

For the diagonal part of (c), expand $\Pi_{M,N}$ from [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. By [def-trf-external-product], $\Delta^*(M\boxtimes N)=M\otimes N$, and similarly with bars. Apply (IV) to $\Delta$: the composite of $\alpha_\Delta$ with $\bar\Delta^*t_{X\times X}$ is $t_X(\alpha_\Delta\otimes\alpha_\Delta)$. After inserting the two factors of $\bar\Delta^*(\alpha_{p_1}\otimes\alpha_{p_2})$, the comparison on factor $i$ is $\alpha_\Delta\circ\bar\Delta^*\alpha_{p_i}=\alpha_{p_i\Delta}$ by (III). Since $p_i\Delta=1_X$ and $\bar p_i\bar\Delta=1_{\bar X}$, this is $1$ on both factors. The result is exactly $t_X$.

For (d), make the compactification reduction of Step 1 and write $a=a_X$, $P=X\times_sX$, and $\bar a=a_{\bar X}$. Let
$$B_M:Rp_{1!}p_2^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*Ra_!M$$
be inverse proper base change in the product square; the barred map is $\bar B$. Its specified normalization is [def-exchange-projection], with invertibility supplied by [prop-functor-package](4). Ordinary mate calculus gives
$$f_XB_M\,b_{p_1}(p_2^*M)\,R\bar p_{1!}\alpha_{p_2}(M)
=\alpha_a(Ra_!M)\,\bar a^*b_a(M)\,\bar B_{f_XM}. \tag{*}$$
Here both sides start at $R\bar p_{1!}\bar p_2^*f_XM$ and end at $f_Xa^*Ra_!M$. To check (*), replace $b_{p_1},b_a$ by the inverses of the ordinary mates using (VI), move those isomorphisms across the equation, and take ordinary adjoints. Expanding the base-change mate formula, both resulting maps are
$$f_P(p_2^*\varepsilon_{a,M})\circ\alpha_{ap_2}(Ra_*M):\bar p_2^*\bar a^*f_sRa_*M\to f_Pp_2^*M.$$
The equality uses precisely $ap_2=ap_1$ and (III), which identifies $\alpha_{p_2}\bar p_2^*\alpha_a$ and $\alpha_{p_1}\bar p_1^*\alpha_a$; naturality moves the counits, and the two adjunction triangle identities cancel the inserted units. This proves the ordinary square used in (4.7), without invoking the differently typed exceptional square.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), left square of (4.7); ordinary-square calculation of Lemma 4.2.1(c1)

proof.text:
Let $e:Ra_!\omega_X\to A_s$ and $\bar e:R\bar a_!\omega_{\bar X}\to A_s$ be the exceptional counits. By definition, $\chi$ has exceptional adjunct $a^*e\circ B_{\omega_X}$, and $\bar\chi$ has adjunct $\bar a^*\bar e\circ\bar B_{\omega_{\bar X}}$. The defining mate formula for $b_a$ and $\delta_X=\bar a^!\iota\circ\beta_a(A_s)$ gives
$$\bar e\circ R\bar a_!\delta_X=\iota\circ f_s(e)\circ b_a(\omega_X). \tag{**}$$
Now the exceptional adjunct of the left side of (d), using the mate formula for $b_{p_1}$, is
$$f_X(a^*e)\,f_XB_{\omega_X}\,b_{p_1}\,R\bar p_{1!}\alpha_{p_2}.$$
Substitute (*) of Step 8, and use naturality of $\alpha_a$ at $e$. This becomes $\alpha_a(A_s)\bar a^*(f_s(e)b_a(\omega_X))\bar B_{f_X\omega_X}$. Equation (**) and $j_X=\alpha_a(A_s)\bar a^*\iota^{-1}$ turn it into
$$j_X\bar a^*\bar e\,\bar a^*(R\bar a_!\delta_X)\,\bar B_{f_X\omega_X}.$$
Naturality of $\bar B$ at $\delta_X$ identifies this with $j_X\bar a^*\bar e\,\bar B_{\omega_{\bar X}}R\bar p_{1!}\bar p_2^*\delta_X$, which is exactly the adjunct of the right side of (d). Bijectivity proves (d). Restriction from the compactifications returns the original maps, completing all four clauses.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(f), right square of (4.7) and exceptional-adjoint conclusion

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 4.2.2(a),(b) and 4.2.4(b),(e),(f), diagrams (4.2)–(4.7); ordinary-square mate calculation 4.2.1(c1) expanded inline; projection indices interchanged

from.place: Proof paragraph (1) and (2): tensor, internal-Hom, unit, diagonal, and dualizing projection comparison identities used in the cohomological trace comparison

split_report.summary: Retained the statement and expanded Varshavsky’s diagram chases into nine steps: proper reduction, the ordinary projection square and exceptional adjunct calculation, Hom uncurrying, the dualizing-unit and biduality argument, diagonal restriction, and the ordinary product-square and counit calculation. Reused existing generic operation/biduality nodes; no new nodes or Mathlib leaves. Corrected an initial draft that omitted the axiom-(V) argument for the unit and confused ordinary with exceptional square exchange. Second reading: explicitly normalized the tensor/exchange maps; justified properness of the compactified product and fixed scheme, extension of arbitrary inputs and restriction coherence; used canonical general biduality in the nondegenerate evaluation argument; corrected the delta typo. No identity or hypothesis changed, and no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: The item has no standalone blueprint node; the steps realize the structural comparison calculations invoked in the proof of lem-trf-local-term-locality and its trace-specialization intermediary.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NL-2ec15f663 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item, all 9 steps, the statement of every cited node, unit sk-i-curve-zero, the parent lem-trf-trace-specialization, and Varshavsky arXiv math/0505564 Lemmas 4.2.1, 4.2.2(a),(b) and 4.2.4(b),(e),(f) with diagrams (4.2)-(4.7). The item statement matches the source clause by clause; (d) has the project's 1<->2 leg swap. The delivery creates no new nodes, and the only related node, lem-trf-cohomological-exchange-calculus (Lemma 4.2.1), does not overlap it. I re-derived every mate calculation myself: the projection square of Step 2, the exceptional adjuncts of Step 3, the uncurrying of Step 4, the evaluation-pairing cancellation of Steps 5-6 (Varshavsky's 4.2.4(b) argument, with thm-fix-general-biduality made explicit), the diagonal identity of Step 7 from (III),(IV), and the (4.7) squares of Steps 8-9. Small cases checked: the point (both (c) and (d) reduce to iota^{-1} iota = 1), identity arrows, and diagonal pullback. The one fault was in Step 5: it computed T at the unit using the counit-defined pi, but T is defined with the compact-support PF^c, so the argument only holds for proper maps.
